chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Segregation in Chicago clubs and restaurants
summary: The Three Deuces took only white patrons and Chicago was prejudiced about restaurants and hotels, which Collins says changed during World War II.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: State and Wacker. Wacker Drive and State Street, in the basement. But no black musicians could come there, you know, clientele, no patrons, black patrons could come there. They'd get run out of there. This was Chicago at that time. It was a terrible -- Chicago really started -- I think the blacks started the upheaval, I should

say, during the war, World War II. But up until that time there were many restaurants that you couldn't go into, you know, they wouldn't serve you. Hotels. You couldn't stay -- Chicago was a terribly prejudiced town. But any way, they had some good bands.
